title: Model Variant Experiment Runner and Safety Ops
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Build an Experiment Runner that lets PMs/Engineers spin up A/B/canary/shadow experiments for model variants with programmable exposure schedules, automated statistical checks, and safety-driven auto-rollback. This is a product-facing orchestration layer + UX on top of the serving runtime so teams can validate quality and performance before full rollouts.

Goals:
- Self-serve experiment creation for model variants (select base model, variant(s), routes).
- Fine-grained exposure control: incremental ramps, per-route caps, and time-windowed exposure.
- Multiple traffic modes: A/B split, sequential canaries, continuous shadowing (no impact on responses).
- Real-time statistical safety checks: both frequentist (sequential monitoring with alpha-spend) and Bayesian checks (credible intervals, posterior prob of win).
- Auto-rollback and mitigation: configurable thresholds on quality/regression signals (eg. lower NPS sim, hallucination rate, latency, token-cost) with automated rollback and staged fallbacks.
- Strong telemetry and audit trail (who started experiment, parameters, outcome, linked PRs & prompts).

High-level design notes:
- Experiment config: JSON schema with fields for variants, exposure schedule (list of [time, pct]), objectives (primary/secondary metrics), statistical plan (test type, stopping rule), and rollback policies. Keep schema minimal but extensible.
- Safety checks: implement two-layer checks: 1) runtime SLO checks (latency p95, error rate) and 2) quality checks (eval-set score deltas, user feedback signals). Both feed into the decision engine.
- Statistical engine: support pre-specified fixed-horizon A/B tests, sequential monitoring using alpha-spend (O'Brien-Fleming) and Bayesian sequential detection (monitor posterior probability that variant > control). Provide guidance in UI for statistical power and minimum sample sizes.
- Auto-rollback: rollback trigger can be immediate (eg. p95 latency spike > 2x baseline) or conditional (eg. quality metric drop > X and sustained for Y mins). On rollback, the system should automatically re-route traffic to last-known-good model and create an incident ticket.
- Shadow traffic: implement forwarding-only path where responses from variant are not returned to users but recorded for offline scoring and drift detection. Must be low-overhead on runtime.
- Exposure safety controls: per-customer or per-API-key caps, global budget for experimental exposure, and daily rate-limits to prevent runaway experiments.

Trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Prefer to keep statistical engine in product layer (not runtime) to enable multiple testing strategies without touching serving code; however, some latency-sensitive SLO checks must run inside runtime telemetry to detect immediate issues.
- Default to conservative alpha and slow ramp profiles for public traffic; let advanced users opt into aggressive profiles.
- Use a hybrid approach for sample size guidance: show frequentist estimate plus Bayesian posterior simulation so teams understand both perspectives.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- UI/CLI to create experiment with variant selection, ramp schedule, and metric selection.
- Backend orchestration that applies traffic routing changes according to schedule and supports pause/resume.
- Runtime telemetry hooks for latency/error SLOs and a separate pipeline for offline quality evaluation (shadowed responses).
- Statistical monitoring that signals when stopping rules are met and outputs human-readable rationale.
- Auto-rollback executor that updates routing, notifies stakeholders, and logs IR (incident record).
- Audit logs and experiment history visible in Console with links to artifacts.

Operational concerns:
- Ensure experiments cannot exceed per-account exposure caps (quota enforcement).
- Retention policy for shadowed responses (30–90 days depending on privacy settings).
- RBAC: only owners or users with Experiment-Edit permission can start/stop experiments.
- Data labeling loop: provide hooks to upload human evals for variant quality scoring.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which default statistical stopping rules to ship first? Proposal: O'Brien-Fleming sequential monitor + Bayesian posterior prob > 0.95.
- Exact UI affordances for metric selection (freeform vs. curated telemetry metrics).
- Rollback communication plan (Slack, email, incident dashboard).
- Performance budget for shadowing — acceptable CPU/memory overhead per request.

Next milestones:
- 2025-02-20: Finalize experiment JSON schema and API prototype (ENG-2891).

acceptance_criteria: Experiment creation UI or API that captures variants, schedule, metrics, and rollback rules
Traffic routing layer honors scheduled ramps and supports manual override
Statistical engine triggers events when stopping rules are hit and logs rationale
Auto-rollback executes within configured 30s of trigger and notifies stakeholders
Shadow mode stores variant responses in secure store with retention policy
Audit trail links experiments to GitHub PRs and console activity logs
